items.title: Proper is finite near a finite fibre (retained with the author's slogan block): for f : X -> S proper with S locally Noetherian and the set-theoretic fibre over s finite, some open neighbourhood V of s has f^{-1}(V) -> V finite.
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter coherent.tex (Cohomology of Schemes)
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28), file coherent.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The neighbourhood argument is complete in the span: a finite fibre makes f quasi-finite at all points above s (morphisms-lemma-finite-fibre); the quasi-finite locus U is open (morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-points-open); its complement Z has closed image since f is proper, so some V through s avoids f(Z); over V the restriction is locally quasi-finite and proper, hence quasi-finite (locally-quasi-compact lemma), has finite fibres (quasi-finite lemma), and is therefore finite by this chapter's characterization card L16381.
